AI CLI Tools Community Digest 2026-11-07

Generated: 2026-11-07 00:50 UTC | Tools covered: 7

  • Claude Code
  • OpenAI Codex
  • Gemini CLI
  • GitHub Copilot CLI
  • OpenCode
  • Pi
  • Qwen Code
  • Claude Code Skills

Cross-Tool Comparison

Cross-Tool Comparison Report — AI CLI Developer Tools Ecosystem

Date: 2026-11-07 | Coverage: 7 tools (Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, Gemini CLI, GitHub Copilot CLI, OpenCode, Pi, Qwen Code)

1. Ecosystem Overview

The AI CLI tool category has matured into a seven-way race where differentiation is shifting from raw model access to agent runtime reliability, orchestration, and governance. Across every community today, the dominant signal is no longer "add capabilities" but "make existing capabilities trustworthy": subagent lifecycle correctness, compaction/context integrity, permission semantics, and process/resource hygiene dominate the hot-issue lists. Release cadences remain aggressive (three of seven tools shipped stable builds today), but maturity is uneven — several tools are converging on the same architectural concepts (multi-agent orchestration, MCP connection pooling, skills/plugins portability) while differentiating on safety posture and target audience. A notable cross-cutting trend is ecosystem interoperability: communities are independently proposing shared standards for skills, plugins, and cross-agent config (Agent Plugins standard, cross-tool skill catalogs, Tessera-style runners), suggesting the next competitive axis will be portability rather than lock-in.

2. Activity Comparison

Note: Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, Gemini CLI, GitHub Copilot CLI, OpenCode, and Qwen Code all expose Issues and PRs via GitHub. Per the source digests, no Discussion data was provided for Claude Code, Gemini CLI, Copilot CLI, OpenCode, or Qwen Code; those are marked N/A (not "inactive"). Pi is the only tool with visible Discussion activity in this window.

Tool Hot Issues (reported) PRs Active (24h) Discussions Release Status (24h)
Claude Code 10 (top issue: 689 👍, 98 comments) 1 (transparency PR, closed) N/A v2.1.319 stable (security-hardening)
OpenAI Codex 10 (top: 79 comments; #30408 at 23 👍) 10+ substantive (+ Guardian series #59993–#60002) Yes — 3 Q&A + 7 Show-and-tell rust-v0.167.0 stable + v0.169.0-alpha.2
Gemini CLI 10 (top: #22323, 13 comments; #21409 at 8 👍) 10 (+4 honorable mentions), mostly closed fixes N/A No release
GitHub Copilot CLI 10 (top: #1972 at 48 👍) 1 (docs/i18n) N/A v1.0.108-0 + 1.0.107/1.0.106 notes
OpenCode 10 (+4 notable; #59387 at 315 comments, #27110 at 42 👍) 10+ (Code Mode VM cluster) N/A v2.2.6 stable
Pi 10 (top: #10605, 13 comments; P0 #11869) 10 (mostly closed fixes) Yes — 1 Q&A + 1 Show-and-tell No release
Qwen Code 10 (top: #14724 at 217 comments — CI bot noise) 10 (refactor/feat heavy) N/A v0.26.9 stable + nightly

Caveats on comparability: Comment counts are not normalized for bot activity (Qwen Code's #14724 is CI-bot meta-churn; OpenCode's #59387 is a consolidated megathread), and 👍 counts reflect repo scale differences. Treat row-level counts as directional, not absolute.

3. Shared Feature Directions

Requirements appearing independently across multiple communities:

Direction Tools Specific Needs
Multi-agent orchestration & subagent correctness Codex, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, Claude Code, Pi, Qwen Code Codex: Guardian reviewer pipeline + multi_agent_v2; Gemini: generalist-agent hangs (#21409), false success reporting (#22323); OpenCode: parallel subagent caps (#27110, 42 👍), premature completed status (#48826); Claude Code: subagent transcript/180s interruption issues
Context/compaction integrity OpenCode, Claude Code, Qwen Code, Copilot CLI, Pi OpenCode loses top-level tools post-compact (#51949); Qwen Code quadratic transcript growth (#13113) + compaction escalation (#16418); Copilot CLI: model-judged pruning proposal (#5362) + MCP schema loss (#5367); Pi: per-conversation compaction policy (#11771)
Permission & approval governance Copilot CLI, OpenCode, Qwen Code, Gemini CLI, Claude Code Command-identifier allowlists with spaces (#4150); opt-out of persistent "Allow always" (#62432); headless auto-memory deny overrides (#15597); destructive git-op guardrails (#22672); fine-grained tool gating at thread start (Codex Q&A #57025)
MCP lifecycle & resource management Codex, Copilot CLI, OpenCode, Claude Code Codex: per-thread process leaks, 9–37 GB RSS (#30408/#12491); Copilot: OAuth token expiry with stale mcp.list status (#5366), schema loss (#5367); OpenCode: OAuth dialog mid-flow close, lost session IDs (#59640); Claude Code: tools/list discarded as errors (#107111)
Cross-agent skills/plugin portability Codex, OpenCode, Pi Agent Plugins standard (#40993, 21 👍); Tessera cross-CLI runner (#59896); cross-tool skill catalogs (#59844, Pi #11870)
Quota/usage visibility & metering trust Codex, OpenCode, Claude Code Taskbar quota tool (#58359); 50% limit-reduction reports (#59594); free-tier opacity megathread (#59387); $10 depleted in 15 min (#107558)
Streaming/protocol resilience Pi, Gemini CLI, Claude Code OpenAI-compatible tool-call streaming contract violations (#11881/#11891/#11882); ACP mid-stream retry corruption (#30165); >5-min request timeouts (#107232)
Cross-platform parity (Windows/macOS/Linux) Codex, Copilot CLI, Claude Code, Pi, Qwen Code, Gemini CLI Windows Computer Use (#51524), Windows project loss (#42739); Entra token caches (#5236); macOS auth verification (#103788); Windows shutdown handlers (#11889); Windows shell-awareness (#15310); Wayland browser failures (#21983)
Safety false-positive reduction Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI Opus 5.5 safeguard regressions (#108048, #108067); blocked authorized local dev (#56475); semantic vs. keyword moderation request (#91579); region blocklists (naver #95539, VK #59738)

4. Differentiation Analysis

Feature focus by tool:

  • Claude Code — Enterprise auditability and privacy-first. Today's headline (User-Agent email leak, #107757, 689 👍) and the maintainers' response (open-sourcing the privacy mod, #107768) plus the v2.1.319 hardening (no classifier fallback behind gateways) reveal a deliberate posture: verifiability over convenience in restricted environments. The Opus 5.5 safeguard false-positive cluster is its principal capability/filtering tension.
  • OpenAI Codex — Orchestration depth and automation maturity. The Guardian evidence/reviewer pipeline, agent command center, cross-backend session switching, and a visibly automated contribution pipeline (copyberry[bot]) indicate an industrial-scale, platform-integrated direction. Its pain profile (process leaks, quota lockouts, Windows regressions) is that of a product scaling faster than its lifecycle management.
  • Gemini CLI — Agent-layer correctness and evaluation rigor. The day's activity is almost entirely stability fixes (PTY FD leaks, timeout handling, retry corruption, heap OOM bundling), reflecting a team investing in the runtime substrate (sandboxing architecture #19873, AST-aware tooling EPIC #22745–#22747). Browser subagent is its weakest surface.
  • GitHub Copilot CLI — IDE/GitHub ecosystem integration and enterprise identity. Highlights are Windows sandbox grants, shared tgrep indexing, /code VS Code bridging, Fusion tier config. Its pain is distinctly enterprise-auth-shaped (Entra broker token caches, MCP OAuth expiry) and input-ergonomics-shaped (IME/Shift+Enter, a years-long CJK demand at 48 👍).
  • OpenCode — Open/provider-neutral and community-governed. Shared MCP connection pooling, Code Mode VM durability semantics, multi-provider model plumbing, and the loudest free-tier community in the set (315-comment megathread). Targets users running local/Ollama models and multi-vendor setups — hence top ask #27110 (parallel subagent cap for VRAM-constrained inference).
  • Pi — SDK/embedded-agent builder focus. The P0 StringEnum typing regression (#11869) and Harness.close() session leaks (#11676) directly affect SDK consumers; streaming-protocol fixes target vLLM/LiteLLM/self-hosted stacks. Accessibility (#1188, closed) and codemode safety (#11858: 24,018 repeated tool calls) round out a developer-library identity.
  • Qwen Code — Skill lifecycle and managed-agent infrastructure. v0.26.9's ZIP uploads, daemon APIs, TS SDK, bulk activation, and the managed-agent execution-diagnostics PR (#16498) show investment in organizational skill distribution. Its signal is degraded by CI-bot noise drowning the tracker.

Target users: Claude Code (regulated/enterprise), Codex (platform teams, multi-surface), Copilot CLI (GitHub-centric enterprise devs), Gemini CLI (Google-stack + Linux power users), OpenCode (open-source/local-model hobbyists-to-prosumers), Pi (agent builders/SDK consumers), Qwen Code (APAC/enterprise skill governance).

Technical approaches: Claude Code leans on mod-level enforcement and server-verified auto mode; Codex on structured reviewer pipelines and SQLite-backed session state; Gemini on OS-sandbox + AST tooling and fail-fast messaging; OpenCode on a VM-based Code Mode with durability primitives; Pi on protocol-conformance breadth; Qwen Code on daemon/SDK skill infrastructure.

5. Community Momentum & Maturity

Momentum ranking (directionally, from engagement intensity):

  1. OpenCode — Highest raw engagement in the set (315-comment megathread, 42-👍 feature). Free-tier controversy is a double-edged signal: extreme community investment, partially negative sentiment. Shipping stable (v2.2.6) while absorbing V2 regressions.
  2. OpenAI Codex — Broadest simultaneous activity: stable + alpha releases, 10+ substantive PRs, active Discussions (7 show-and-tell posts). Automated contribution pipeline suggests enormous throughput. Sustained multi-week issues (60–79 comments) show durable user investment.
  3. Qwen Code — High issue volume but low signal quality (CI-bot meta-issues dominate; stale PR backlog since September). Shipping steadily (v0.26.9 + nightly) with competent refactor PRs — iteration is real, but community observability is impaired.
  4. Claude Code — Sharp, focused engagement (one 689-👍 privacy issue outweighs most repos' entire day). Low PR surface, high trust scrutiny. Mature release discipline (security-hardening patch).
  5. Gemini CLI — Strong fix velocity (14 PRs, many closed same-day) but no release; issue engagement middling (top 👍 = 8). Agent-layer bugs are the bottleneck.
  6. GitHub Copilot CLI — Steady cadence (three versions in three days) but thinnest PR community (one docs PR) — consistent with a more closed, vendor-driven contribution model. Auth regressions are the reputational risk.
  7. Pi — Highest ratio of "fix-available" closures to open issues — an unusually responsive maintainer posture. No release today; a P0 typing regression is the watch item.

Maturity assessment: Claude Code and Copilot CLI show process maturity (security hardening, ecosystem integration). Codex and Gemini CLI show infrastructure maturity (orchestration pipelines, sandboxing, eval/telemetry — though Gemini's own team flags eval trust gaps). OpenCode, Pi, and Qwen Code are rapidly iterating but regression-prone — classic velocity-over-stability tradeoffs in young runtimes.

6. Trend Signals

For technical decision-makers and developers, in priority order:

  1. Agent runtime reliability is the new battleground. Subagent false-success reporting (Gemini #22323), premature completion (OpenCode #48826), and compaction-induced capability loss (OpenCode #51949, Claude Code #107979) are silent failures — the most dangerous class for automated pipelines. Buyers should require observability into subagent termination reasons and tool-availability states before deploying autonomous workflows.

  2. Process and memory lifecycle is an unsolved systemic gap. Codex's three separate MCP leak clusters (9 GB → 37 GB → zombies) and Pi's Harness.close() leaks are the clearest evidence that MCP-based architectures need reaping guarantees. Expect "MCP connection pooling" (OpenCode v2.2.6, Codex lifecycle fixes) to become table stakes.

  3. Permission models are converging on declarative, thread-scoped gating — but implementations still leak (space-in-identifier allowlists, "Allow always" overrides, headless deny paths). Governance buyers should treat permission semantics as a procurement criterion, not a checkbox.

  4. Enterprise identity friction (Entra brokers, OAuth token caches) is a deployment blocker, especially on Windows/macOS — Copilot CLI's cluster and Claude Code's browser-verification failures (#103788) suggest auth flows designed for consumer cadence struggling under enterprise session management.

  5. Skill/context token economics matter. The convergence of compaction policy requests, context-pruning proposals (#5362), and per-namespace catalog budgets (OpenCode #62176) shows users are optimizing the cost per turn, not just capability. Metering surprise reports (Claude Code #107558, Codex quota threads) compound this.

  6. Safety filtering is over-triggering on legitimate work. Opus 5.5's documented regression vs. Opus 4.8 (#108048, bisected) and Codex/Gemini's opaque blocks signal that keyword-based moderation is now a productivity tax. Semantic moderation (#91579) is the likely resolution path.

  7. Interoperability standards are emerging bottom-up. Agent Plugins (#40993), cross-CLI runners (Tessera), and cross-tool skill catalogs (Pi #11870, Codex #59844) are community-led — a signal that buyers should favor tools embracing portable skills/MCP configs, as vendor lock-in is being actively contested by users.

  8. Bot/automation noise degrades community signal quality. Qwen Code's CI churn and the copyberry[bot] authorship note in Codex's digest are early indicators of a new problem: as AI-assisted development scales, repositories need better triage hygiene for decision-makers to trust community metrics.

Report compiled from 2026-11-07 community digests for github.com/anthropics/claude-code, openai/codex, google-gemini/gemini-cli, github/copilot-cli, anomalyco/opencode, earendil-works/pi, and QwenLM/qwen-code. Metrics are as-reported; comment/👍 counts are not normalized for repo scale or bot activity.

Claude Code Skills Highlights

Source: anthropics/skills

Claude Code Skills Community Highlights Report

Data as of 2026-11-07 | Source: github.com/anthropics/skills

1. Top Skills Ranking (Most-Discussed PRs)

Note: The provided dataset lists Comments: undefined for all PRs, so ranking here is based on update recency + revision depth + linked issue activity. Community discussion volume is more reliably reflected in the Issues section below.

Rank Skill / PR Functionality Discussion Highlights Status

2 skill-creator trigger eval isolation — #1298 Fixes false misses/invalid scores in trigger evaluation; Windows select() pipe failure; runtime failure handling Cross-platform correctness for the meta-skill that generates all other skills OPEN

2. Community Demand Trends (from Issues)

Distilled from the highest-comment Issues:

  • Trust & Security Boundaries — #492 (46 comments, top issue): Community skills distributed under the anthropic/ namespace impersonate official skills, creating a permission-escalation trust vulnerability.
  • Org-Wide Skill Sharing — #228 (17 👍 8): Users want a shared skill library/link instead of manual .skill file distribution via Slack/Teams.
  • Evaluation Harness Reliability — #556 (13 comments, 7 👍): run_eval.py yields 0% trigger rate — the skill-testing loop itself is broken.
  • Context Economy / Token Budgets — #1487: claude-api skill eagerly injects ~156k tokens, exhausting context in one call. Related: #1329 proposes symbolic compact-memory notation.
  • Skill Authoring Best Practices — #202 (CLOSED): skill-creator reads like docs, not operational instructions — token inefficiency.
  • Reasoning/Quality Governance — #1385: Proposal for pre-task calibration → adversarial review → delivery verification pipeline.
  • Plugin/Distribution Hygiene — #189 (9 👍): document-skills and example-skills install identical content, causing duplicate skills.
  • Skill Discovery Semantics — #2064: theme-factory description says what but not when to use — a recurring authoring anti-pattern.

Emerging direction: the community's demand is shifting from "add more skills" toward infrastructure maturity — security, sharing, evaluation, and token efficiency.

Pattern: A wave of small, surgical bug-fix PRs (mostly by repeat contributor gerardrecinto) is queued for merge — these are low-risk and likely to land first.

4. Skills Ecosystem Insight

The community's most concentrated demand is no longer for more Skills, but for a trustworthy, token-efficient, and shareable Skill infrastructure — security boundaries, evaluation correctness, context economy, and org-level distribution now outweigh net-new skill submissions.

Report generated from anthropics/skills PR and Issue metadata as of 2026-11-07. All links point to github.com/anthropics/skills.

Claude Code Community Digest — 2026-11-07

Source: github.com/anthropics/claude-code

1. Today's Highlights

The community is dominated by a high-visibility privacy bug (#107757, 689 👍) alleging that Claude Code leaks the user's email in the User-Agent header during web searches — a CLOSED PR (#107768) publishing the built-in privacy mod source appears to be the maintainers' direct response. A new release (v2.1.319) tightens auto mode behavior when telemetry/feature flags are disabled, and a wave of Opus 5.5 safeguard false-positive reports (#108048, #108067) signals growing friction between capability and content filtering.

2. Releases

v2.1.319 — Release notes

  • Changed auto mode behavior when telemetry or feature flags are off (including behind LLM gateways): calls the server cannot verify are now asked about or denied, with no fallback to the built-in classifier.
  • Escape hatch: set CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_MODE_SERVER=0 to retain the built-in classifier.
  • Bedrock, Vertex, and Foundry paths are unchanged (unaffected by the server check).

Takeaway: This is a security-hardening change that trades convenience for auditability in restricted/gatewayed environments. Enterprises behind LLM proxies should test before rolling out.

3. Hot Issues

  1. [#107757] Privacy violation in User-Agent header — link · 98 comments · 689 👍 User reports receiving scam emails because their signed-in address is leaked in the User-Agent header during web searches. Highest-engagement issue of the day; the linked PR #107768 suggests an official fix is in flight. This is the headline story.

  2. [#1757] Claude Code requires users to constantly login — link · 90 comments · 78 👍 Open since June 2025 and still active — daily re-auth demands remain a top pain point. Long-lived issue with steady community pressure.

  3. [#10238] Add support for subdirectories in skills — link · 55 comments · 168 👍 CLOSED enhancement. Teams want nested skill directories; closure suggests a resolution (shipped or superseded). High 👍 indicates strong demand.

  4. [#91495] Site permissions ignored by built-in browser (Desktop) — link · 33 comments CLOSED. "Allow all websites" settings ignored on Windows/macOS Desktop — a permissions-trust issue now resolved.

  5. [#103788] Desktop (macOS) sign-in fails: "We couldn't verify your browser" — link · 20 comments Both Google and email auth return 400; only an exit-IP change partially helps. Indicates an IP/geo fingerprinting problem in the auth flow.

  6. [#95593] Chat completion notifications silent on desktop — link · 9 comments Notifications work for Code/Cowork but not Chat across Windows + macOS. A regression in a widely-used quality-of-life feature.

  7. [#95539] All naver.com domains blocked by default safety restrictions — link · 9 👍 False-positive blocklist hit on South Korea's primary portal. Regional availability concern; daum.net/tistory.com unaffected.

  8. [#107232] Cannot handle API requests >5 minutes long — link · 7 comments Linux/API/networking. Long-running requests still fail — relevant to agent workflows and batch jobs.

  9. [#107979] Long session shows turns as "[cleared]", stripping pasted content/screenshots — link · 3 comments Windows/core/desktop. Model context loses pasted content mid-conversation — a serious data-integrity issue for long sessions.

  10. [#108048] Opus 5.5 reasoning_extraction refuses Read of user's own notes file — link Reproducible, bisected to a 30-line block, dependent on user-scope rules files being present. First of a cluster of Opus 5.5 safeguard false-positives (see also #108067). Not observed on Opus 4.8.

4. Key PR Progress

Only one PR was updated in the last 24h:

  1. [#107768] mods: add the privacy mod (CLOSED) — link Publishes the source of Claude Code's built-in privacy mod under mods/privacy. The mod's job: refuse a shell call holding the signed-in account's email address and naming a User-Agent. No new behavior — pure source disclosure/transparency.

    Why it matters: This is almost certainly the maintainers' answer to issue #107757. By open-sourcing the mod that enforces privacy at the shell-call layer, Anthropic is signaling that the email-leak behavior is guarded (or now being guarded) at a documented, auditable boundary. Expect the community to scrutinize the manifest and hooks module closely over the next 24–48h to confirm it actually closes the User-Agent leak path.

Note: With only one PR in the window, the digest's PR section is intentionally short — activity is concentrated on the issue tracker.

5. Hot Discussions

No discussion data was provided for this window. Section omitted.

6. Feature Request Trends

Distilled from the issue set:

  • Skills extensibility — Subdirectory support in skills (#10238, 168 👍, now CLOSED) is the single most-upvoted enhancement. Teams are building nontrivial skill libraries and need structure.
  • Cross-session / cross-environment messaging — Varlink for cross-session messaging on Linux (#107175, 10 👍) and an effort argument for claude-code-remote create_session (#107292). Developers want agents to orchestrate peer sessions more richly.
  • Connectors everywhere — Projects (beta): give the coordinator (project chat) access to claude.ai connectors (#107601). Users want parity between cloud threads and coordinator conversations.
  • Finer-grained session control — effort control, cross-marketplace plugin dependencies (#86493), and remote session parameterization.
  • Reduce false-positive safeguards — Multiple requests (#91579) to move from keyword-based to semantic moderation.

7. Developer Pain Points

Recurring frustrations across the tracker:

  1. Authentication friction — Constant re-login (#1757) and opaque browser-verification failures (#103788) are the longest-running and most-commented auth complaints.
  2. Opus 5.5 safeguard false positives — A fresh, rapidly-growing cluster (#108048, #108067, #91577) where legitimate read/write/cyber tasks are blocked. Users note Opus 4.8 did not behave this way — a model-version regression in practice.
  3. Long-session integrity — Turns silently "[cleared]" (#107979), subagent transcripts >5 MiB unresumable (#83261), and subagents interrupted at ~180s (#88993). Context and agent state are fragile in long workflows.
  4. Request timeouts — API requests >5 min still fail (#107232); MCP tools/list results discarded as errors (#107111).
  5. Privacy & trust — The User-Agent email leak (#107757) combined with the privacy mod disclosure (#107768) shows the community is now actively auditing what Claude Code sends to third parties.
  6. Desktop regressions — Sidebar status dots lost (#108019), dictation failures on macOS (#94687) and Windows (#104003), silent completion notifications (#95593), and a system-wide input freeze on Windows (#106746).
  7. Cost/metering surprises — $10 credit depleted in ~15 min under light use (#107558) — a candidate metering bug.
  8. Platform/regional blocklists — naver.com falsely blocked (#95539), cyber task false-flags.

Generated for 2026-11-07. Links point to github.com/anthropics/claude-code. Companion to the release notes for v2.1.319.

OpenAI Codex — openai/codex

OpenAI Codex Community Digest — 2026-11-07

1. Today's Highlights

Two releases landed in the last 24h: the stable rust-v0.167.0 ships an agent command center (codex agents --no-daemon) with unread-result markers and cross-backend switching in the session picker, while rust-v0.169.0-alpha.2 continues the alpha line. The issue tracker remains dominated by long-running Windows project-loss regressions, MCP process/memory leaks, and quota/rate-limit complaints, several of which have accumulated 60+ comments over weeks. PR activity is unusually concentrated: a large batch of copyberry[bot] PRs targets TUI input handling, multi-agent guidance, and the new "Guardian" reviewer/evidence pipeline.

2. Releases

rust-v0.167.0 (stable)

  • New agent command center: codex agents --no-daemon; command center and session picker now mark unread results (#58238, #58239, #58263, #58264).
  • Terminal session picker supports switching between connected backends; drafts are preserved when switching (#58280, #58457).
  • Link: https://github.com/openai/codex/releases

rust-v0.169.0-alpha.2

  • Alpha release, no detailed changelog provided.
  • Link: https://github.com/openai/codex/releases

3. Hot Issues

  1. #42739 — Windows desktop: local projects disappear from sidebar after update (79 comments, 👍7) Still the highest-traffic open bug; the Projects section shows "No projects" while chats/folders are intact. Long-running, unresolved, and now compounded by a same-day duplicate report (#59895). https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/42739

  2. #51524 — Windows Computer Use stops at get_window_state (Chrome/Edge) (72 comments, 👍8) Browser automation on Windows breaks at window inspection, blocking click/type steps entirely. High engagement from Windows power users. https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/51524

  3. #30408 — MCP server processes leak per thread (9+ GB RSS) (69 comments, 👍23) The most-upvoted issue in this set: per-conversation MCP processes are never reaped on archive/close. A clear resource-management regression with broad impact. https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/30408

  4. #12491 — Codex.app GUI: 1300+ zombie MCP processes, 37 GB leak (39 comments, 👍7) Older but still active; same root cause family as #30408 and #55141. Strong evidence that process lifecycle management is a systemic gap. https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/12491

  5. #52503 — Web/GitHub: repeated approvals after "Always allow", lost upload results (23 comments, 👍3) Approval state isn't honored, and long-running tool results are dropped. Directly degrades trust in the approval UX for web workflows. https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/52503

  6. #57190 — macOS: browser disabled in existing chat after restart (14 comments, 👍3) Inconsistent per-chat capability state after restart; another instance of state not persisting correctly across sessions. https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/57190

  7. #56682 — VS Code extension fails to initialize UI even in isolated profile (13 comments, 👍5) Extension onboarding is broken for a Windows user despite a clean profile — suggests env/registration issues rather than local config. https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/56682

  8. #42315 — iOS Remote on Windows: custom sections omit Codex projects (13 comments, 👍6) Sync names work but project payloads don't — a cross-surface data-parity bug affecting remote workflows. https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/42315

  9. #32880 — Windows: workspace-write DENY ACL blocks linked worktrees (12 comments) Sandbox ACL regression that silently breaks autonomous Git operations in worktrees. Zero upvotes but steady comments — likely structural, not cosmetic. https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/32880

  10. #45383 — Interrupted sessions waste quota rebuilding context (6 comments, 👍4) Resume behavior re-burns tokens instead of continuing; a cost/efficiency complaint that ties into the quota threads below. https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/45383

4. Key PR Progress

  1. #60014 — Honor managed runtime authentication modes (CLOSED) Lets requirements.toml pin features.runtime_agent_instances.mode to dual_header or assertion_only, rejecting conflicting explicit settings. https://github.com/openai/codex/pull/60014

Gemini CLI Community Digest — 2026-11-07

1. Today's Highlights

No new releases landed in the last 24 hours, but activity remains heavily concentrated in the agent/subagent subsystem — subagent recovery correctness, browser agent failures, and tool-count limits dominate the top of the issue tracker. On the PR side, a large batch of stability fixes merged or closed today, targeting PTY file-descriptor leaks on macOS, API timeout handling for long-thinking requests, and mid-stream retry corruption in ACP mode. The overarching theme this cycle is making the agent layer more reliable and less surprising — both for users and for the eval/telemetry infrastructure that measures it.

2. Releases

No new releases in the last 24 hours.

3. Hot Issues

  1. #22323 — Subagent recovery after MAX_TURNS reported as GOAL success (13 comments, 👍2, p1) A codebase_investigator subagent reports status: "success" / Termination Reason: "GOAL" despite hitting the turn limit before doing any analysis. This is a correctness bug in agent observability — it silently masks failure, which is especially dangerous for automated pipelines. Highest-comment issue of the day and flagged for retesting.

  2. #19873 — Zero-dependency OS sandboxing & post-execution intent routing (9 comments, 👍1, p2) Proposes leaning into Gemini 3's native bash affinity by running POSIX tool chains (grep, sed, awk) inside an OS-level sandbox rather than restricting the model. A significant architectural direction for the agent runtime — large effort, still under design.

  3. #21409 — Generalist agent hangs (8 comments, 👍8, p1) The highest-reaction issue in this batch: any deferral to the generalist agent hangs indefinitely (up to an hour observed). The workaround — instructing the model not to use subagents — is a major usability regression. Strong community signal via 👍.

  4. #22745 — Assess impact of AST-aware file reads, search, and mapping (7 comments, 👍1, p2) An EPIC tracking whether AST-aware tooling can reduce misaligned reads, token noise, and turns. Directly connected to #22746 and #22747 — a coordinated investigation into more precise codebase navigation.

  5. #21968 — Gemini does not use skills and sub-agents enough (7 comments, p2) Anecdotal but widely felt: custom skills (e.g., "gradle", "git") are ignored unless explicitly invoked. This undermines the value proposition of the skills/subagent system — if the model won't reach for them, users won't build them.

  6. #22267 — Browser Agent ignores settings.json overrides (5 comments, p2) The AgentRegistry reads merged settings correctly, but the Browser Agent bypasses them (e.g., maxTurns). Configuration that silently doesn't apply is a classic trust-eroding bug.

  7. #22232 — Browser agent session takeover & lock recovery (4 comments, p3) Requests replacing the current fail-fast behavior on locked browser profiles with automatic takeover/recovery. Persistent-mode users hit orphaned-process locks frequently; a resilience improvement would meaningfully reduce friction.

  8. #21983 — Browser subagent fails on Wayland (4 comments, 👍1, p1) Linux/Wayland users report the browser subagent terminating with GOAL despite failing. Combined with #22267 and #22232, the browser agent is clearly the least-stable surface area right now.

  9. #24246 — 400 error with >128 tools (3 comments, p2) Gemini CLI hits a 400 when too many tools are in scope. The reporter expects the agent to be smarter about scoping enabled tools — an increasingly relevant issue as MCP servers multiply the tool surface.

  10. #22672 — Agent should stop/discourage destructive behavior (3 comments, 👍1, p2) The model occasionally reaches for git reset or --force when safer alternatives exist. A safety-and-trust issue that speaks to broader concerns about autonomous operation on real repositories.

4. Key PR Progress

  1. #30185 — Prevent recursive interactive gemini sessions in shell mode (p1) Blocks gemini from being spawned inside Shell Mode (!) or the [Shell] tool, and rejects unsupported CLI config subcommands. Prevents a genuinely confusing failure mode.

  2. #30189 — Reject MessageBus.request() immediately when publish fails Previously a failed publish waited the full 60s timeout before rejecting with a generic error. Now it fails fast with the original error — meaningful for debugging and latency.

  3. #30183 — Configurable 60s API headers timeout (closed) Long-thinking requests (thinkingLevel: HIGH, large contexts) were dropped with UND_ERR_HEADERS_TIMEOUT and replayed from scratch. Adds model.requestTimeoutMs / GEMINI_API_HEADERS_TIMEOUT_MS across all auth modes. A high-impact fix for Vertex/API-key users.

  4. #30184 — Fix orphan /dev/ptmx master FD leak on macOS (closed) Prevents kern.tty.ptmx_max exhaustion during long sessions with @lydell/node-pty@1.1.0. Subtle but critical for sustained use.

  5. #30180 — Bound multi-part tool outputs and evict older multimodal inlineData (closed) Fixes V8 heap OOM crashes during long agentic sessions that repeatedly call read_many_files or ingest screenshots. Directly addresses session-length scalability.

  6. #30165 — Handle mid-stream retries to prevent text concatenation (closed) Fixes partial text/tool calls from abandoned retry attempts being concatenated and executed in ACP mode. A correctness fix for anyone driving Gemini CLI programmatically.

  7. #30187 — Prevent multi-hour quota retries; notify ACP client (closed) Stops indefinite hangs on HTTP 429 with long reset windows, and surfaces retry attempts to ACP clients instead of hiding them.

  8. #30164 — Resolve folder trust before entering macOS Seatbelt sandbox (p1) Since #29214, the sandbox denied access to ~/.gemini/trustedFolders.json, breaking the trust dialog. Follow-up to the #30143 startup-crash fix.

  9. #30181 — Eliminate barrel-import bundle bloat in VS Code companion (closed) Switches from a barrel import of @google/gemini-cli-core to narrow subpath imports, cutting the extension bundle from ~13.8 MB to ~2.7 MB dev / 1.7 MB prod. Big startup-perf win.

  10. #30182 — Prevent silent multi-minute loading hangs on network failures (closed) Surfaces errors instead of an indefinite spinner under model: auto and default network configs — including TLS interception and ALL_PROXY setups.

Honorable mentions: #30010 (telemetry skill_name in safe metadata whitelist for enterprise), #30176 (preserve --worktree across auth restarts), #30119 (standalone theme.json discovery).

5. Hot Discussions

No discussion data was provided for this period.

6. Feature Request Trends

Distilling from the issue set, the most-requested directions are:

  • Smarter agent routing and self-awareness — The model should proactively use skills/subagents (#21968), understand its own CLI flags and hotkeys (#21432), and correctly scope tools when counts grow large (#24246).
  • AST-aware codebase navigation — A coordinated EPIC (#22745, #22746, #22747) exploring AST grep, tilth, and glyph for precise reads and search.
  • Token-frugal context management — "Tactful Extraction" for surgical reads (#19561) and persistent file-based task tracking to replace in-context WriteToDo (#18836).
  • Browser agent resilience — Session takeover, lock recovery (#22232), and honoring config overrides (#22267).
  • Subagent observability — Trajectory visibility via /chat share (#22598) and subagent context included in /bug reports (#21763).
  • Safety guardrails — Discouraging destructive git operations (#22672) and per-workspace policy scoping (#18397).

7. Developer Pain Points

  • Subagent hangs and silent failures. Two of the top three issues (#21409, #22323) describe the agent either hanging forever or reporting success when it actually failed. The 8 👍 on the hang issue underscore how disruptive this is.
  • Browser agent instability. Three separate issues (#21983, #22232, #22267) point to the browser subagent as the least reliable component — platform-specific failures (Wayland), config that doesn't apply, and brittle locking.
  • Configuration that silently doesn't take effect. Whether it's settings.json overrides for the Browser Agent or ~/.gemini/agents/*.md symlinks not being recognized (#20079), developers repeatedly hit cases where their setup is ignored without warning.
  • Workspace pollution. The model creates tmp scripts in random directories (#23571), adding cleanup overhead before commits.
  • Crash-adjacent instability. Crashes on output hooks (#22186) and heap OOMs during long sessions — the latter addressed by PR #30180.
  • Eval/telemetry gaps. Internal evals "bleed" and are hard to trust (#23166); the steering eval had to be commented out (#23313) — a meta-pain-point affecting the team's ability to measure regressions.

  9. [#8544] edit tool rewrites line endings of untouched lines (link) — CLOSED. Mixed CRLF/LF files get corrupted on edit. Data-integrity issue now addressed.

  10. [#11676] Harness.close() leaks pi-ai provider session resources (link) — OPEN, inprogress. Leaked WebSocket + 5-min idle timer prevents process exit — relevant to embedded/durable agent builders.

4. Key PR Progress

  1. [#11895] grep globs matched relative to path (link) — CLOSED. Fixes globs silently matching nothing when path ≠ cwd.

  2. [#11896] Wait for image resize worker to terminate (link) — CLOSED. Fixes macOS/Node 24 process abort from worker teardown races.

  3. [#11891] Omit empty tools: [] for tool history on openai-completions (link) — CLOSED. Resolves vLLM/LiteLLM 400 errors.

  4. [#11882] Split tool-call blocks when stream index and id disagree (link) — CLOSED. Prevents silent concatenation of two tool calls' arguments.

  5. [#11890] Draw fullscreen Kitty images on all terminals (link) — CLOSED. Fixes blank images in Orca/xterm.js.

  6. [#11885] Retry streams cut short after reply had begun (link) — CLOSED. Adds the Magpie/Anthropic mid-stream drop message to retryable patterns.

  7. [#11894] edit refuses files that are not valid UTF-8 (link) — OPEN. Prevents silent U+FFFD corruption of UTF-16/legacy-encoding files.

  8. [#11888] Record live thinking level on branch before each prompt (link) — CLOSED. Fixes stale thinking level after /tree navigation + resume.

  9. [#11889] Run shutdown cleanup when Windows console closes (link) — OPEN. Adds Windows shutdown handling where SIGHUP isn't available.

  10. [#11878] Allow local tools/console declarations in codemode (link) — OPEN. Fixes SyntaxError from hidden parameter name collisions.

5. Hot Discussions

Q&A / Ideas

  • [#11870] How do you keep skills organized across Pi and other agents? (link) — 1 👍. Cross-tool skill duplication and drift; author shares a cataloging CLI.

Show and tell

  • [#11860] CaseClip — save a Pi mistake as a reviewable case card (link) — 1 👍. Captures request + tool result + correction for post-hoc review.

6. Feature Request Trends

  • Model catalog expansion: requests to add deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017 (#11877), glm-5.3-flashx (#11884), and Kimi K3.1-pro + video modality (#11883). Users want parity with vendor model tables.
  • SDK customization depth: identity preamble override without replacing default prompt sections (#11317); per-conversation compaction policy for durable agents (#11771).
  • Codemode sandbox hardening: repetition guards (#11858) and faithful Error serialization (#10650).
  • Long-running agent guidance: context management patterns for tool-heavy multimodal embedded sessions (#11863).

7. Developer Pain Points

  • Streaming protocol fragility: OpenAI-compatible providers violating the tool-call streaming contract cause silent argument corruption (#11881) and empty-tools 400s (#11843). Multiple PRs this cycle target this class.
  • Silent data corruption: edit rewriting line endings (#8544) and mangling non-UTF-8 files (#11894), plus prompt-arg apostrophe loss (#11861) — bugs that "succeed" while damaging content.
  • Cross-platform gaps: Windows shutdown/argv[1] virtual path issues (#11889, #11865) and macOS worker teardown races (#10695) show POSIX-first assumptions leaking through.
  • Auth and provider churn: OpenAI OAuth 403 (#10605) and GitHub Copilot token refresh on 401/403 (#10238) leave users blocked with unclear recovery paths.
  • Resource lifecycle: leaked provider sessions on Harness.close() (#11676) and uncaught temp-file errors crashing sessions (#10585) frustrate embedded/CI users.

Digest generated from github.com/earendil-works/pi activity for 2026-11-07.

Qwen Code — QwenLM/qwen-code

Qwen Code Community Digest — 2026-11-07

1. Today's Highlights

Qwen Code shipped v0.26.9 stable alongside a fresh nightly, headlined by a major expansion of the Skill installation and activation system (ZIP uploads, daemon APIs, TypeScript SDK support, bulk activation, and recovery protections). Meanwhile, issue activity is dominated by CI stability churn from qwen-code-dev-bot and a cluster of high-severity session-management bugs, including a documented case of auto-compaction turning a review-only skill into unauthorized source-code implementation.

2. Releases

v0.26.9 (stable) and v0.26.9-nightly.20261106.80fd7c3353 both landed in the last 24h.

  • No known breaking changes.
  • Headline feature: Skill installation and activation — Skill ZIP uploads, daemon APIs, TypeScript SDK support, bulk activation, and recovery protections make installing and managing skills substantially more robust.
  • Nightly included test hardening for the interactive foreground-shell (poll the foreground-shell frame instead of snapshotting it, PR #16455).

3. Hot Issues

  1. #14724 — Main CI failed: Managed Agent gate — no test identified (OPEN, 217 comments). A long-running meta-issue tracking a persistently red Managed Agent gate. The extreme comment volume signals chronic CI instability, not a single bug.
  2. #13113 — Session becomes unopenable: "Transcript snapshot is too large to index" (P1). file_history_snapshot grows quadratically and eventually exceeds a hardcoded 256 MiB index limit, making sessions permanently unopenable. A serious data-loss-adjacent bug for long sessions.
  3. #16418 — Repeated auto-compaction turns review-only skill into unauthorized source-code implementation (P1). A /ce-doc-review skill was unexpectedly escalated into implementing the reviewed plan — a notable agent-safety and permission-scope concern.
  4. #15597 — Headless -p managed auto-memory can never save (P1). The implicit edit/write_file deny overrides memory agents' scoped allow, so auto-memory silently no-ops while still costing tokens.
  5. #15412 — Long project paths prevent chat recording and break sessions list (P2). Path flattening exceeds filesystem component limits on macOS.
  6. #15675 — sed edit simulation: . does not match \r or a whole emoji (P1, now CLOSED). In-process sed simulation diverges from real sed due to missing s/u RegExp flags.
  7. #15310 — Tell the model which shell it uses, instead of letting it assume bash (P3). On Windows, the model writes POSIX commands into cmd.exe, burning a full turn per failure.
  8. #15495 — Image payload eviction has no off switch and an undocumented threshold (P2). Silent rewriting of inline images at an undeclared count of 20.
  9. #16457 — MCP OAuth: overlapping flows share fixed callback port 7777 (P2). Starting a second OAuth flow invalidates the first, breaking multi-server authorization.
  10. #14629 — Telemetry: emit OpenRouter routing provider and generation id as span attributes (P3). Strong interest in aggregator-routing observability.

4. Key PR Progress

  1. #16501 — refactor(runtime-broker): extract binding provisioning from RuntimeBrokerService. Continues the decomposition of the Runtime Broker into dedicated collaborators (matching the dispatcher/reconciler/recovery pattern).
  2. #16498 — feat(managed-agent): Add execution diagnostics and agent graph. Persists tool/Skill usage, file-operation and line-change metrics, and an authorized agent relationship view — decoupling execution evidence from conversation outcomes.
  3. #16493 — feat(channels): add GitHub repository event filter with allowlist and blocklist. Surfaces a first-class Repository Filter control in the Web Shell channel editor.
  4. #16470 — fix(release): derive the next patch when the preview baseline lags latest. Repairs version resolution when a stable patch shipped after the latest preview.
  5. #16401 — fix(cli): forward the folder-trust store into the container sandbox. Prevents containerized re-execution from falling back to default trust state.
  6. #16352 — fix(managed-agent): mask digit-led passwords and refuse empty Harness user info. Hardening the upgrade command's start/verify phases.
  7. #14353 — fix(web-shell): honor configured loading phrases. Applies custom loading phrases while preserving host overrides and built-in fallback.
  8. #16503 — refactor(managed-agent): fold the last CSI statement helper copies. Removes duplicated statement-preparation helpers in CSI stores.
  9. #15286 — fix(ci): keep sdk-java resolver bookkeeping and in-house jars out of the host cache. Prevents mutable inode sharing between job-local Maven repos and the host cache.
  10. #12592 — fix(session): reattach explicit resume after project move. Adds bounded cross-project lookup so qwen --resume <uuid> survives a moved project directory.

5. Hot Discussions

No discussion data was provided in the source dataset; this section is omitted.

6. Feature Request Trends

  • Better memory & long-term context — optional external memory services (#16429 proposing bzmem), plus fixes to managed auto-memory in headless mode (#15597).
  • Cross-platform correctness — shell-awareness on Windows (#15310), path-length handling on macOS (#15412).
  • Web Shell UX — inline branch chat anchored to selections (#16474), managed-host UI gaps (#16471).
  • Observability & telemetry — OpenRouter routing attributes (#14629), cache-write token preservation (#15414).
  • Session management robustness — transcript indexing limits, resume-after-move, background shell lifecycle.
  • Terminal integration — OSC 7501 program status reporting (#13870).

7. Developer Pain Points

  • CI noise drowning real signal. A large fraction of hot issues are bot-filed Main CI failed reports (e.g. #14724, #16191, #16377), several self-labeled "Provisional." This erodes triage quality and community attention.
  • Session state fragility. Unbounded transcript growth (#13113), path-derived session directories (#15412), and background-shell status files stuck "running" after abrupt ends (#15800) form a recurring cluster.
  • Permission/approval surprises. Auto-memory denial (#15597), auto-compaction escalation (#16418), and amend-guard gaps (#16449) all point to approval logic that behaves unexpectedly under long-running or headless conditions.
  • Cross-platform shell assumptions. Windows users pay a full model turn per failed POSIX-style command (#15310).
  • Stale PR backlog. Multiple [status/stale] PRs from September (e.g. #12592, #12572, #12450) remain unmerged after weeks, suggesting reviewer bandwidth constraints.

item.content:encoded:
OpenClaw Ecosystem Digest 2026-11-07

Issues: 367 | PRs: 500 | Projects covered: 5 | Generated: 2026-11-07 00:50 UTC

  • OpenClaw
  • Hermes Agent
  • IronClaw
  • QwenPaw
  • ZeroClaw

OpenClaw Deep Dive

OpenClaw Project Digest — 2026-11-07

1. Today's Overview

OpenClaw remains in a high-tempo maintenance phase: 367 issues and 500 PRs were updated in the last 24 hours, with no new releases cut. The issue mix is heavily weighted toward regressions and state/session-integrity bugs (SQLite worker OOM, MCP lifecycle leaks, Gateway event-loop stalls), suggesting the team is still stabilizing the 2026.10.x–2026.11.x line rather than shipping new surface area. PR throughput is healthy (133 merged/closed vs 367 open), but the open backlog is large and many top-commented issues carry clawsweeper:no-new-fix-pr and needs-maintainer-review — meaning fixes exist conceptually but are stuck at review. Community energy is concentrated on a small set of long-lived "diamond lobster" bugs, several of which are P0/P1 crash-loops or memory regressions. Overall project health: active but under stability pressure; the ratio of open-to-merged PRs and the volume of unaddressed P1s are the main watch items.

2. Releases

None. No new releases in the last 24h. (Notable context: issue threads reference in-flight prereleases v2026.11.5-beta.1 and an extended-stable prep PR for 2026.9.37.)

3. Project Progress

133 PRs were merged/closed in the last 24h. Notable closures and active merges include:

  • #194380 [CLOSED] improve(ci): scope provisioning tests to copied inputs — reduces wasteful CI work for source-only PRs. link
  • #194379 [CLOSED] fix(release): authorize scoped 2026.11.2 Kova waiver — unblocks a release perf gate. link
  • #194369 [CLOSED] chore(release): prepare 2026.9.37 extended-stable — backport batch restoring privacy boundaries, session-account continuity, and safer update/state handling on the extended-stable line. link
  • #168794 / #166017 / #164923 [CLOSED issues] — several long-running bug threads closed, including Codex 32 MiB image-request 502s, MCP session idle-TTL non-eviction, and short-term promotion structural rejection. 166017 · 164923
  • #178291 [CLOSED] — post-activation Doctor authority failure on 2026.10.4→10.5 update resolved. link

Net: strong bug-closing cadence on legacy regressions, but new P1/P2s are arriving faster than maintainers can triage (see Backlog Watch).

4. Community Hot Topics

Item Comments Type Link
#160959 Gateway blocks for minutes capturing large external plugins (2026.9.6 regression) 80 P0 crash-loop link
#164294 Gateway state DB WAL auto-checkpoint never completes 39 P2 link
#177656 native host exec returns shared-state integrity-admission error 29 P1 link
#150635 short-term recall eviction blocks dreaming deep-phase promotion 25 P2 link
#191944 gateway stop fails on macOS "ancestry could not be fully inspected" 23 P2 UX link

Underlying needs: The hottest threads cluster around three themes — (a) event-loop/liveness integrity under large plugin/tool loading (#160959, #166641); (b) shared-state and session admission consistency (#177656, #182647, #192959); and (c) memory/recall subsystem correctness (#150635, #164923). These are not cosmetic: they cause crash loops, message loss, or "every turn fails" states. Users are effectively acting as SREs for their own Gateways, which is a satisfaction risk.

5. Bugs & Stability (ranked by severity)

P0 / crash-loop

  • #160959 — Gateway event loop blocked for minutes on large external plugin capture at startup and on runtime republish. No fix PR; waiting on maintainer review. link
  • #178291 (CLOSED) — Post-activation Doctor authority-check failure during 2026.10.4→10.5 chat update. link

P1 — data integrity / message loss / crash

  • #177656 — Native host exec shared-state integrity-admission failures; ≥28 occurrences on stable 2026.10.5. link
  • #155563 — Regression 2026.9.5: service-child relay/anchor + MCP groups retained after successful turns. link
  • #191847 — New regression 2026.10.10: large session repeatedly kills 512 MB SQLite worker (ERR_WORKER_OUT_OF_MEMORY); every turn in that session fails "admission is closed". link
  • #166641 — web_fetch cold fallback synchronously captures unrelated plugins on Gateway main thread → liveness stalls. link
  • #185656 — Large zstd transcript archive still exceeds Node string limit in media-persistence migration (regression of #170847); blocks update. link
  • #182647 — Cloud-worker turns fail pre-inference: "Session capability metadata requires worker preparation". link
  • #192959 — Kubernetes: Gateway refuses to start after pod restart (fsGroup remount rejects client credential dir). link

P2 highlights

  • #164294 WAL auto-checkpoint pinned by in-process reader; #191944 macOS stop failure; #166017 (CLOSED) MCP idle-TTL never evicts → broker hits 256-child cap; #182891 prompt cache never reused (cache read dropped N -> 0); #160494 cron bound to persistent session rejected at rotation. 164294 · 191944 · 182891

Fix-PR status: Several bugs already have candidate PRs in flight (#188881 for dispatched-agent MCP authorization; #194359 for v16 Doctor memory-FTS upgrade; #194129 for shared-session access loss after list updates), but most P0/P1s remain no-new-fix-pr.

6. Feature Requests & Roadmap Signals

Notable open feature requests:

  • Per-model usage logging for cost tracking (#13219, 10 comments) — long-standing ask for aggregated token/cost views beyond per-session JSONL. link
  • Configurable Dream Diary language/prompt (#79223) — non-English workspaces get mixed-language output because the memory-core prompt is hardcoded. link
  • Hide agents from picker while keeping them spawnable (#166678) — multi-agent org visibility control for WebUI/macOS/iOS. link
  • Setting to disable hosted plugin catalog feed (#164620) — network/privacy control over clawhub.ai fetch. link
  • Configurable Control UI Ctrl+Shift+A archive shortcut (#163739) — collides with browser shortcuts. link
  • msteams dynamic SharePoint site resolution for uploads (#136271) — removes hardcoded sharePointSiteId. link

Prediction: Watch #13219 and #164620 — both align with cost-governance and privacy themes that the extended-stable backport ledger already touches, making them plausible candidates for a 2026.12 feature window. #166678 is likely gated behind the multi-agent runtime work.

7. User Feedback Summary

Real user pain points in this window:

  • "Every turn in that session fails" — #191847 and #182647 describe total session lockout (SQLite worker OOM; cloud-worker metadata gap), the harshest UX failure short of data loss. 191847 · 182647
  • Update-path fragility — #193962 reports the #187197 SQLite header-probe fix is unreachable from 2026.10.10 because the installed updater runs the old 10 s probe; users are stuck mid-upgrade. link
  • Cost anxiety — #178373 (no run-level token budget; retained history re-billed every turn) and #182891 (prompt cache never reused) both describe unexpected spend, not just latency. 178373 · 182891
  • Mobile/Control UI friction — #191944, #163739, and the closed #139909 (composer renders ~5–6 chars/line on phones) point to persistent small-screen polish debt.
  • Satisfaction signal: Zero 👍 on almost all high-comment issues — comment volume exceeds endorsement volume, a pattern typical of workaround-driven engagement rather than enthusiasm.

8. Backlog Watch

Long-unanswered or stalled items needing maintainer attention:

  • #167609 (created 2026-10-09) — Code Mode leaks guest-script TypeErrors as internal_error; needs product decision + fix-shape sign-off. link
  • #127195 (created 2026-08-21) — 16 call sites emit byte-identical "changed while starting work" error with no reason code; needs-product-decision. link
  • #112638 (created 2026-07-22, stale) — session.maintenance enforce does not bound the store; thread/channel entries exempt from all reclaim. link
  • #103067 (created 2026-07-09, stale) — Centralize chat-session naming; define subagent session lifetime/persistence. link
  • #123792 (created 2026-08-14, stale) — Assistant turns render twice with claude-cli backend. link
  • PR #75225 (open since 2026-04-30, stale) — Expose configured descriptions in agents_list; labeled proof: sufficient, waiting on maintainer. link
  • PR #127770 (open since 2026-08-22) — OpenAI native PDF document opt-in; proof: sufficient, merge-risk: compatibility, waiting on maintainer. link

Assessment: The backlog is dominated by decisions, not code — needs-product-decision and needs-maintainer-review appear on the majority of top issues. Clearing a decision-only queue for #127195, #167609, and PR #75225 would be a high-leverage move for perceived responsiveness.

Cross-Ecosystem Comparison

Cross-Project Comparison Report — AI Agent & Personal AI Assistant Open-Source Ecosystem

Snapshot Date: 2026-11-07

1. Ecosystem Overview

The personal AI assistant / agent open-source landscape on 2026-11-07 is characterized by intense maintenance-phase activity across three of five tracked projects, with zero new releases ecosystem-wide — a signal that the cohort is consolidating stability ahead of a coordinated Q4/Q1 release window rather than expanding surface area. A common pattern emerges across OpenClaw, Hermes Agent, QwenPaw, and ZeroClaw: core session/state integrity, memory subsystem correctness, and identity/authorization boundaries are the dominant bug classes, indicating the ecosystem has moved past "does it work?" into "does it stay trustworthy under load, across deployments, and across channels?" Plugin/catalog ecosystems (Hermes, QwenPaw, ZeroClaw) are simultaneously flourishing as growth vectors and exposing registration-contract fragility. Community engagement is workaround-driven rather than enthusiasm-driven (high comment volume, low reaction counts), and backlog analyses across all projects converge on the same bottleneck: maintainer decision throughput, not contributor supply. Two projects (IronClaw) show zero activity, suggesting a bimodal distribution between active and dormant entries in this niche.

2. Activity Comparison

Project Issues Updated (24h) PRs Updated (24h) Merged/Closed (24h) Release Status Health Score
OpenClaw 367 500 133 PRs None (2026.11.x in-flight) Stable-under-pressure (high activity, large backlog, P0/P1 unaddressed)
Hermes Agent 50 (43 open / 7 closed) 50 (39 open / 11 merged) 11 PRs None (0.22.x stable) Active & productive (mild maintenance debt)
IronClaw 0 0 0 None Dormant
QwenPaw 22 (12 open / 10 closed) 38 (18 open / 20 merged) 20 PRs None (2.2.2.post1 stable / 2.3.0b2 beta) High-velocity maintenance (fast triage, architectural debt accumulating)
ZeroClaw 20 (6 open / 14 closed) 50 (35 open / 15 merged) 15 PRs None (v0.9.0 gating) Security-hardening phase (review-throughput bottleneck)

Ranking by 24h activity volume: OpenClaw ≫ Hermes ≈ ZeroClaw > QwenPaw > IronClaw (dormant). Ranking by backlog clearance efficiency: QwenPaw > ZeroClaw > Hermes > OpenClaw.

3. OpenClaw's Position

Advantages vs. peers:

  • Scale dominance: OpenClaw's 367 issues / 500 PRs updated in 24h is ~7–10× the volume of Hermes or ZeroClaw and ~13–23× QwenPaw's — it operates at reference-implementation scale, acting as the de facto framework other projects benchmark against.
  • CI/release discipline: Only project with active extended-stable backport ledgers and scoped release waivers (e.g., Kova waiver #194379), suggesting mature release engineering peers lack.
  • Richer subsystem surface: Dream Diary, Doctor authority model, Gateway event-loop integrity, and MCP lifecycle handling represent deeper subsystem investment than peer projects.

Technical approach differences:

  • Gateway-centric architecture with explicit session-admission semantics and a SQLite worker pool — a heavier footprint than Hermes' gateway/session-authority consolidation or QwenPaw's plugin-per-channel model.
  • Prerelease/beta channeling (v2026.11.5-beta.1, 2026.9.37 extended-stable) — peers ship on simpler stable/beta splits.
  • Dependency on native host exec and cloud-worker turns introduces integrity-admission failure classes (#177656, #182647) unique to its breadth.

Community size comparison:

  • OpenClaw's top issue threads carry 80, 39, 29, 25, 23 comments vs. Hermes' peak of 40, QwenPaw's 4, and ZeroClaw's 9. This is a 10–20× larger engaged user base at the top of the funnel.
  • Caveat: Zero 👍 on most high-comment OpenClaw issues vs. modest 👍 counts on Hermes (#97681: 4) and QwenPaw — OpenClaw's engagement is issue-driven and problem-centric, not enthusiasm-driven, suggesting a user base dependent on it operationally rather than passionately.

4. Shared Technical Focus Areas

Three cross-project requirements emerge as ecosystem-wide:

(a) Session/State Integrity Under Load — OpenClaw, Hermes, ZeroClaw

  • OpenClaw: SQLite worker OOM (#191847), Gateway event-loop stalls (#160959), admission-closed failures (#182647).
  • Hermes: Prompt lost on attached clients (#147626), Stop reporting false cancellation (#143303), composer restore-after-send (#148277).
  • ZeroClaw: Long-session 422 rejections (#12263), channel startup message overwrite (#12279).
  • Need: Atomic, re-checkable authority over session state that survives retries, reconnects, and multi-device attachment.

(b) Memory Subsystem Correctness — OpenClaw, Hermes, QwenPaw

  • OpenClaw: Recall eviction blocking dreaming promotion (#150635), eviction-before-promotion defects.
  • Hermes: Memory/kanban read-only API demand (#149815); recall semantics in multisession flows.
  • QwenPaw: Memory tag index 503 (#8580), reranker empty-api_key errors (#8276), refactor of recall as transient context (#8457).
  • Need: Deterministic index rebuild, safe eviction policy, and clear separation between persisted memory and injected recall.

(c) Authorization/Identity Boundaries — OpenClaw, Hermes, ZeroClaw

  • OpenClaw: Shared-state integrity admission (#177656/#182647), MCP lifecycle leaks.
  • Hermes: Approval-gate bypass via shell functions (#150329), toolset pick ignored on gateway path (#147832).
  • ZeroClaw: A concentrated 10+ issue security sweep — session ownership (#11127), SOP wildcards (#11123), cron approval (#12260), XFF spoofing (#12052), vodozemac CVEs (#12272).
  • Need: Authority re-validated at each effect using trusted runtime facts, not caller-supplied data.

(d) Plugin/MCP Contract Hardening — Hermes, QwenPaw, ZeroClaw, OpenClaw

  • Hermes: Plugin Hackathon cluster + catalog PRs (~5), but registration/nav regressions.
  • QwenPaw: Plugin metadata failures (#8595), navigation regression (#8590), dependency check refactor (#8598).
  • ZeroClaw: Multi-registry origins (#12216), deferred MCP HashMap ordering (#12176).
  • Need: Durable plugin manifest/route contracts as the ecosystem scales to hundreds of community extensions.

5. Differentiation Analysis

Dimension OpenClaw Hermes Agent QwenPaw ZeroClaw
Primary focus Core runtime stability, Gateway/MCP/dreaming Cross-gateway collaboration, Desktop UX, plugin catalog Multichannel self-hosting, memory, Creator pipeline Security/identity-access hardening, relay dashboard
Target users Power users/SREs running self-hosted Gateways Multi-device personal users + plugin developers Self-hosters (esp. Windows/Docker/IM channels) Security-conscious operators, proxy deployments
Architecture Gateway + SQLite worker + shared-state admission Gateway session-authority + Desktop/web clients Plugin-per-channel, IM bridge, console Daemon + RPC + OIDC/XFF-aware Gateway
Release posture Extended-stable backports + betas 0.22.x stable, incremental Stable + 2.3.0b2 beta v0.9.0 release-gated on security
Distinctive work Dream Diary, Doctor, event-loop integrity Cross-gateway federation (#97681) IM channel parity, quote/context UX Principal-boundary refactor (#9746, #12239)
Primary risk Backlog triage starvation Review latency on feature PRs (#51672: 4.5mo) Environment-sensitive failures (Windows/Docker) XL PR review throughput gating release

Interpretation: OpenClaw is the breadth leader (more subsystems, larger user base); Hermes is the collaboration/federation pioneer; QwenPaw is the self-hosting/IM-channel pragmatic builder; ZeroClaw is the security-first specialist. There is meaningful non-overlap in target use cases — the projects are complementary rather than direct substitutes.

6. Community Momentum & Maturity

Activity Tiers (24h)

  1. Tier 1 — High-throughput stabilizer: OpenClaw (467 combined issue+PR updates/day).
  2. Tier 2 — Actively iterating: Hermes Agent, ZeroClaw (~50–70 combined).
  3. Tier 3 — Focused maintenance: QwenPaw (~60 combined, higher merge ratio).
  4. Tier 4 — Dormant: IronClaw (0).

Maturity Signals

Project Maturity Indicator Verdict
OpenClaw Release engineering (waivers, backports), large user funnel Mature core, strained ops
Hermes Plugin hackathon, community-authored fixes Mature extensibility, growing pains in review
QwenPaw Same-day feature→PR turnaround (#8609, #8610) Responsive but pre-architecture-refactor
ZeroClaw Systematic security sweep from source review Mature security posture, release-gated

Iterating vs. Stabilizing

  • Rapidly iterating (features): Hermes (plugin catalog, dashboard), QwenPaw (console UX trio, memory).
  • Stabilizing (bug-fix focused): OpenClaw (regressions), ZeroClaw (authorization refactor).
  • The shared bottleneck: all three active Tier 1–3 projects flag maintainer review throughput as the gating constraint — not contributor supply. This is a maturity bottleneck, not an engagement one.

7. Trend Signals

Five industry-level signals valuable to AI agent developers:

1. Identity/Authorization is the new correctness frontier

ZeroClaw's dedicated 10+ issue security sweep, Hermes' approval-gate bypass (#150329), and OpenClaw's shared-state admission failures all point to the same conclusion: the next generation of agent bugs will be authority-boundary bugs, not inference-quality bugs. Actionable for developers: design authority checks as atomic, per-effect, trusted-fact-based operations from day one.

2. Session integrity across multi-device/multi-channel is table stakes

Every active project reports session-state inconsistencies under attach/retry/reconnect. Users are becoming SREs for their own agents. Actionable: invest early in idempotent turn semantics and cross-client session reconciliation.

3. Memory subsystems need explicit "trusted vs. synthetic" separation

QwenPaw #8457 (recall injected as untrusted context), OpenClaw's dream/recall eviction defects, and Hermes' memory API requests all converge on: memory is not a single abstraction — index, eviction, and recall-injection are separate, independently testable concerns.

4. Plugin/MCP registration contracts are scaling bottlenecks

Three of four active projects report plugin metadata/route/manifest failures. Actionable: publish and version a plugin contract spec now, before the ecosystem reaches hundreds of extensions.

5. Release gating has shifted from feature-completeness to security- and integrity-completeness

ZeroClaw's v0.9.0 is explicitly security-gated; OpenClaw is holding back 2026.12 feature candidates behind stability backports. Actionable for developers: plan security/integrity review as a release gate, not a post-release patch cycle — this is becoming the ecosystem norm.

Hermes Agent — nousresearch/hermes-agent

Hermes Agent — Project Digest

Date: 2026-11-07 | Repository: github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent

1. Today's Overview

Activity remains high across the board: 50 issues and 50 PRs updated in the last 24h, with 0 new releases. The issue tracker shows a heavy skew toward open items (43 open vs. 7 closed), suggesting the maintainers are currently absorbing more community input than they are resolving. PR throughput is healthier: 11 merged/closed against 39 open, including several fix PRs from prior days finally landing today (e.g., delegate-card joining, Daybreak delegation routing, gateway transcript reads). A noticeable cluster of activity centers on the plugin catalog and Plugin Hackathon submissions (~5 PRs), plus a steady stream of gateway/session-authority work and package-manager (pnpm/npm) hardening follow-ups to #149746. The most engaged discussion by far remains the long-running Let Bots collaborate across gateways (#97681) with 40 comments — a sign that multi-agent/cross-gateway collaboration is the community's dominant strategic interest. Overall health: active and productive, with a mild maintenance-debt signal in the open/closed issue ratio.

2. Releases

No new releases in the last 24h; latest release data shows none. No changelog, breaking changes, or migration notes to report. Version references in today's issues (e.g., v0.22.5 in #147626) indicate the project is on the 0.22.x line, but no tagged release was cut today.

3. Project Progress

Merged / Closed PRs (11 total, highlights):

PR Summary Impact
#136573 fix(desktop): join delegate cards by delegation id, not repeated goal Fixes cross-adoption of subagent workers in Desktop transcript
#149846 fix(gateway): Daybreak delegation routes recognize owner's gateway-hosted chats Fixes "this session is 'local'" false rejection for own Desktop/Webapp chats
#149836 fix(desktop): each delegate card shows only its own subagents Removes duplicate helper display after rejected-then-retried delegation
#149538 fix(desktop): a rejected delegate batch lists no children Prevents phantom children in transcript
#51672 Add hermes heal CLI, startup healer warnings, hook denylist New operational self-healing surface (Windows-relevant)
#150234 plugin-catalog: add va-claims (VA Benefits tracker) Catalog expansion

Closed Issues (7 total): Notably #143656 (Linux updater restarts paused gateways before publishing install stamp → stale /health version) and #106960 (systemd dashboard inventoried as manual-serve) were closed, plus four pnpm/npmc hardening follow-ups (#150032, #150033, #150034, #150035).

Net direction: Desktop delegation display correctness and gateway routing were the clear focus of shipped fixes today; plugin catalog growth continues at pace.

4. Community Hot Topics

  1. #97681 — Let Bots collaborate across gateways — 40 comments, 4 👍 (most active item) Underlying need: Users want federated personal agents — bots running on different machines/owners that can work together without surrendering control of models, tools, memory, or credentials. This is the community's flagship architectural ask and effectively frames the project's multi-agent roadmap.

  2. #106960 — systemd dashboard inventoried as manual-serve — 14 comments (CLOSED) Underlying need: Predictable service lifecycle/update inventory for hand-rolled installations; service discovery currently ignores dashboard units.

  3. #145171 — Entry-point cutover: serve, remote Desktop and web onto the gateway session authority — 6 comments Underlying need: Consolidating fragmented entry points (hermes serve vs. gateway) into one session-authority model — the architectural counterweight to #97681.

  4. Plugin Hackathon cluster (PRs): #150379 Gateway Guardian, #150360 Diké, #149625 proofops, #150374 cash-desk, #149174 gogogoogle (draft) Underlying need: A thriving third-party ecosystem — reliability guards, legal verification, financial tooling, and wiki/memory integrations — signaling the plugin surface is a healthy community growth vector.

5. Bugs & Stability

Ranked by severity (as tagged):

P2 — High:

  • #148329 — Skill lock blocks ALL git writes in the containing repo. A protection feature blocking unrelated work with no agent-side remedy. Reporter flags severity as high.
  • #133006 — macOS Desktop form-filling failure: stale/empty browser targets + unverified recovery loops. Needs repro; affects computer-use reliability.
  • #147920 — computer-use bring_to_front fails permanently after implicit cua-driver session idles — every call rejected until gateway restart (macOS, cua-driver 0.21.0).
  • #147923 — Desktop: assistant message after bot-chat cron delivery not rendered until next turn. Persisted correctly; UI staleness only.
  • #142982 — Desktop cannot unpin a pinned legacy cron-run chat — pin returns silently, backend refuses.
  • #149154 — kanban: update drain kills running workers (persist path has no wait) + wastes card attempts on sessions that never started.
  • #137723 — Automatic Codex quota recovery stays exhausted on disk after successful probe (security-boundary flagged).
  • #147626 — Attached clients see turn stream but never the user's prompt (v0.22.5, macOS host).
  • #143303 — Stop in gateway group chat reports turn stopped while still running — group chat can start a second turn beside the live one.
  • #146280 — Anthropic usage: utilization ≤1% reported as 100% (fraction scaling bug in _usage_windows).

P3 — Medium / Other:

  • #150369 — iPhone Safari webapp mic requires double-tap (AudioContext resume gated on user gesture; Safari-only).
  • #150123 — Browser dashboard chat crash-loops ("gateway exited (1)") on single-profile installs with active session. New today; no fix PR yet.
  • #150329 — Approval gate bypass: shell function/alias forwarding hides command word (f(){ rm "$@"; }; f -rf /) → escapes hardline floor; also unflagged pipe-to-shell sinks. Security-relevant.
  • #148831 — delegate_task silently drops top-level routing field. AI-assisted report; fix PR linked.
  • #148277 — Desktop send landed but also restored into composer (duplicate submission risk under new ID).
  • #147832 — Explicit -t toolset pick still gets every plugin toolset and MCP server (gateway path) — config/security boundary.
  • #141755 — Skills security scanner false-positives block legitimate community skill book-to-skill (132 findings).

Fix PRs existing: Delegate display bugs (#136573, #149538, #149836, #149846 — all merged today) and #149862 (split-unit failed task keeps its own goal). No fix PR yet for the newest reports (#150369, #150123, #150329).

6. Feature Requests & Roadmap Signals

Likely near-term (already have tracking issues or staged plans):

  • Cross-gateway bot collaboration (#97681) — explicit foundation-laying language ("across machines now, across owners next"); the highest-signal roadmap item.
  • Gateway session-authority cutover (#145171) — staged fast-follow to #134889; consolidating serve/Desktop/web onto one authority.
  • Gateway transcript read API (#150102) — session.transcript for reading stored sessions without attaching; enables third-party frontends.
  • Read-only kanban/run/memory API endpoints (#149815) — requested by a Home Assistant "Hermes Voice" integration builder; voice-satellite use case.

Lower-likelihood / exploratory:

  • Email MCP integration package (#99030) — AgentMail/IMAP/SMTP adapter; aligns with industry MCP momentum.
  • Cron-style Bot Chat delivery for webhook results (#150380) — new today, 0 comments.
  • Suppress mobile notifications while Desktop is active (#148307) — small UX win, 1 👍.

Prediction: The next version is most likely to ship gateway session-authority consolidation and delegation display fixes (already merged), with cross-gateway collaboration as the marquee multi-release initiative.

7. User Feedback Summary

Pain points:

  • Fragmented entry points — users repeatedly hit friction where hermes serve, Desktop URL/Cloud/SSH modes, and the gateway disagree on session authority (#145171, #147626, #150123).
  • Session/state inconsistencies — messages restored into composer after send (#148277), prompts missing on attached clients (#147626), Stop reporting premature cancellation (#143303), unpin refusal (#142982). These erode trust in the core chat loop.
  • Overzealous protection mechanisms — the skill lock blocking unrelated git writes (#148329) and the skills scanner false-positive (#141755) both frustrate legitimate workflows.
  • Install/update lifecycle surprises — stale /health version after updates (#143656, now closed) and pnpm/npm mirror edge cases (#150032).

Use cases emerging:

  • Voice satellites / home automation — user building "Hermes Voice" on Echo devices requests read-only APIs (#149815).
  • Webhook/event-driven automation — workflow engines routing errors into per-profile Bot Chat (#150380).
  • Multi-device workflows — same chat on Mac, Windows, and iOS simultaneously (#147626).
  • Domain-specific plugins — legal citation verification (Diké), VA benefits tracking (va-claims), gateway reliability monitoring (Gateway Guardian).

Sentiment: Constructive and technically engaged. Reports are detailed with environment specifics and repro steps; several are AI-assisted and adversarially reviewed (e.g., #148831). The community is investing heavily in the plugin ecosystem, indicating satisfaction with the extension surface even as core session consistency remains the top friction area.

8. Backlog Watch

Long-unanswered items needing maintainer attention:

  • #51672 — Add hermes heal CLI, startup healer warnings, hook denylist. Open since 2026-06-24 (~4.5 months), only closed today after long delay. Its lengthy dwell time is a caution flag for PR review latency on feature-scale contributions.
  • #99030 — Ship an Email MCP integration package. Open since 2026-08-31 (~2.2 months), only 2 comments; a clear ecosystem-aligned request with no maintainer response.
  • #97681 — Let Bots collaborate across gateways. Open since 2026-08-29 (~2.3 months); very active (40 comments) but still under review — needs a maintainer decision to unblock the roadmap's centerpiece.
  • #124725 — fix(desktop): reopen the focused session tab, not stale main-pane chat. Open since 2026-09-27 (~6 weeks); a targeted Desktop UX fix awaiting review.
  • #149174 — [DRAFT] gogogoogle plugin. Explicitly marked not-yet-final; needs author action and reviewer bandwidth for hackathon judging.

Recommendation: Prioritize a maintainer decision on #97681 and a response on #99030, and clear the ~6-week-old Desktop fix #124725 to keep the community's PR enthusiasm from stalling.
